regions.full_page: Father Guardian and Brother Cook brought me to Fort Wayne to catch the Golden Arrow Train on the Pennsylvania, which if on schedule would reach Chicago in time to catch the widely advertised Hiawatha on the "Milwaukee". Ithad snown that morning however, and that meant a probable delay in the train service. Sure enough, the Conductor on taking our ticket as we left Fort Wayne lamented their being 25 minuete late, which meant that if they didn't lose any more time in 150 miles to Chicago, we'd make the said Hiawatha and thus reach St. Paul about 7 P.M. On leaving Huntington, however, we had said the Rosary for a favorable trip and safe return and, thanks be to God, I just forgot a- bout worrying that day. The Milwaukee management kindly consented to wait till they got my ticket, though they advised against bothering a- bout a "clergical permit". Mildred and Jean Conley were there and the O'Donnells: - had been trying in my absence to procure said clerical permit, but without success. I forget if I took dinner on the train but I did take a small lunch, a glass of milk, I believe .25 cents, and was in good shape for a worth- while supper - and a night's rest when we got to St. Paul. Then only, however, it was that I learned the particulars about the place, time etc. of the Funeral. Grandma Conley with Helen, and John, instead of whiffing me away, stressed that I get back on the train and they with me, went on to Minneapolis. There I should take another train an hour or so later, for Ortenville 200 miles further on; say Holy Mass next morning and thence, go with the Pastor, dear Father George Campbell, by auto the balance of the trip, 20 miles to Graceville. ...
